messages:
maya: thinking out loud — ops-friendly experiment idea: run aggressive quant profiles (int8 / 4-bit) during off-peak windows and keep a shadowed int8 pipeline on for peak traffic to gather micro-eval signals. rough config sketch:
```
quant.schedule:
  window: '02:00-06:00'
  profiles: [fp8, int8, 4bit]
  shadow: true  # run shadow path in parallel for live signal
  retention_days: 7
```
would cut unit cost overnight and give us real traffic signal to catch regressions before we promote profiles. thoughts? :thinking_face:

Sam: big +1 on cost but flag: retrieval-heavy endpoints will see embedding drift. tiny numeric shifts => big recall changes. we need embedding-drift detectors + per-customer thresholds. also private deployments might forbid shadowing raw traffic.

Lin: agree with Sam. propose adding micro-eval gating and a "quality escrow" per-endpoint. workflow: shadowed results run through micro-eval set (retrieval + few-shot QA), compute degradation score. if score > threshold revert to baseline fp16. escrow = allowed deg-budget for a rollout. store profile provenance hash in model metadata.

Jon: metrics we should capture for the gating: embedding_cosine_90p_delta, token_perplexity_delta, latency_p95, cost_delta, retrieval_recall_topK_drop. shadow logs -> where do we persist them? parquet to s3 or stream to telemetry topic for batch jobs?

maya: plan: shadow -> ephemeral parquet partitions into s3 -> consumer job runs micro-evals and writes metrics to telemetry. default retention 7 days; enterprise customers can opt for longer. for private deployments we provide a local agent that computes micro-evals in-situ and emits aggregated metrics only (no raw PII).

deploy-bot: Canary started: endpoint=/v1/generate cluster=eu-2 profile=int8-shadow triggered_by=@maya

ops-oncall: +1 on auto-fallback. add this to the runbook: https://runbook/quant-fallbacks — if degscore > threshold: 1) notify oncall, 2) auto-rollback to pinned fp16, 3) trigger nightly retest. Also flag alerting for embedding drift at lower threshold so SRE sees slow regressions. :thumbsup:

Sam: additional suggestion — for embeddings we should try re-centering (SVD) calibration offline on a small canonical corpus before promoting a profile. helps reduce systematic bias from quant noise.

Lin: also: "quality escrow" helps commercial: sales can sell cheaper profiles with a bounded degradation SLA. implement as simple counter: each failed micro-eval consumes N points; if escrow exhausted -> autoswitch. keep escrow metadata as string on endpoint config (hashable).

maya: action items: 1) maya - draft RFC with schedule + fallback-flow + privacy constraints, 2) Lin - define escrow schema + API, 3) Sam - assemble micro-eval sets for retrieval endpoints, 4) Jon - add metrics & telemetry sinks. goal: RFC + prototype canary by EOW.

Jon: EOW sounds doable. I'll add ingestion matchers and a parquet writer for shadow streams.

maya: thanks everyone — I'll open the RFC PR today and tag the infra/security folks for the private-deploy constraints.

Sam: one more note — make sure to include a small calibration harness for embeddings in the RFC so backend teams can run it during canaries.

Lin: agreed. also include a short section about provenance (profile hash, quant-toolchain-version, calibration snapshot id).

maya: noted. I'll include a sample gating matrix and a minimal config example for enterprises.

ops-oncall: reminder: add an oncall runbook snippet for manual forcing of escrow reset for billing disputes.

maya: will do. closing thread for now — will post RFC link once PR is up. :raised_hands:
